title: api-gateway: tuning streaming proxy buffers, routing rules, and payload limits for OpenAI-compat
author: Alex Morgan
body: Context: Several Redwood customers reported intermittent streaming stalls and elevated tail latency when using the OpenAI compatibility layer with multi-tool/function-calling prompts. Root cause analysis showed three contributing factors: (1) conservative default streaming proxy buffers causing head-of-line delays under backpressure, (2) routing rules that selected legacy, higher-latency backends for certain tool-enabled requests, and (3) payload size validation that rejected or truncated structured outputs produced by tool-calls when downstream proxies added headers. This PR proposes coordinated runtime and config adjustments to improve streaming stability, preserve structured output in tool/function calling flows, and maintain OpenAI-compat behavior. Changes: - Increase streaming proxy internal buffer from 64KB -> 256KB and add adaptive flush thresholds based on observed downstream ACK timings. - Introduce a new route attribute "tool_calling_optimized" and update routing rules to prefer low-latency inference pools for requests that include tool/function-calling headers or OpenAI-style "function_call" fields. - Relax payload validation to allow larger structured outputs when content-type is application/json-stream and record original payload size in tracing for debugging. - Add a compatibility shim in openai_adapter.go to preserve OpenAI-style streaming chunk delimiters when the request is proxied through the gateway. - Add telemetry: new metrics streaming_proxy.buffer_fill_ratio, routing.decision.reason, and api.payload_truncation.events. - Include feature flag (api.gateway.streaming_adaptive_buffers) to gate adaptive buffer behavior for canary rollouts. Testing: - Unit tests covering buffer flush semantics and payload validation changes (streaming_buffer_test.go). - Integration test that replays a customer incident trace with tool-calling conversation and verifies no stalls and that structured output arrives intact (test_streaming_proxy.sh). - CI initially failed due to flaky integration test; increased test timeouts and improved a mock backend to be deterministic. Final CI run: all checks passed. Notes: - This change intentionally raises buffer sizes; we added buffer_fill_ratio metrics and a SLO dashboard tile to monitor memory impact. - Routing rule update preserves backwards compatibility by using the new attribute only when requests explicitly indicate tool/function-calling behavior; default routing unchanged. - Feature-flagging allows a phased deploy to Dedicated clusters and then to hosted API. Checklist: - [x] Add adaptive buffer implementation and defaults - [x] Update routing decision logic and add route attribute - [x] Preserve OpenAI streaming delimiters in compat layer - [x] Add metrics and dashboards - [x] Add integration + unit tests - [x] Docs and compatibility notes updated Related: linear/ENG-2148, support/SUP-1187.
commit_summary: Implemented adaptive streaming buffers, routing preference for tool-calling requests, relaxed payload validation, OpenAI streaming delimiter shim, added metrics and tests
review_thread: Priya Nair: Can we add a feature flag for the adaptive buffer change so we can roll this out?
Alex Morgan: Added api.gateway.streaming_adaptive_buffers flag and defaults.yaml entry; docs updated to show how to enable per-cluster.
Liam Chen: The routing change looks good but we should ensure the decision is deterministic and cached for short TTL to avoid evaluating heavy predicates per request.
Alex Morgan: Implemented a 30s in-memory route-decision cache and added routing.decision.reason metric to trace when cache misses happen.
Sofia Patel: Integration test flaked in CI (timing), suggesting we need a more deterministic mock backend. Please re-run CI after fix.
Alex Morgan: Reworked the mock backend to use fixed latency distributions and increased test timeout; CI green on rerun.
Priya Nair: Approval provided after canary plan and dashboards added.
release_notes: Improved API Gateway streaming stability and OpenAI compatibility: increased adaptive proxy buffers, routing optimizations for tool/function-calling requests, and preserved structured streaming output. Feature-gated adaptive buffers for phased rollout.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag api.gateway.streaming_adaptive_buffers=false by default in Hosted. Run canary in Dedicated clusters with flag=true. Monitor streaming_proxy.buffer_fill_ratio and api.payload_truncation.events; rollback if memory pressure observed.
impact_summary: Reduces streaming stalls and tail latency for tool-enabled/structured output flows. Adds modest memory overhead when adaptive buffers are enabled; telemetry added to monitor impact. Routing change improves latency for function-calling paths without affecting existing routes unless request indicates tool usage.
